clue.text: Youngster bound to get smart with Mr Dodd

parts.note: to bound is to leap, to spring
smart in the sense of stylish, chic
Ken Dodd was a famous British comedian from Liverpool

explanation.surface: A lad leaps up to dress smartly alongside a famous comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a much-loved British comic, so 'Mr Dodd' gives KEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring chicken is an idiom for a young, inexperienced person.

clue.text: Lecture on investment designed to increase confidence

definitions.text: Lecture on investment designed to increase confidence

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed below, so the lecture follows the investment

parts.note: a PEP was a Personal Equity Plan, a British tax-free investment
a lecture is a talk

explanation.surface: A speech about investing meant to boost morale.
explanation.walkthrough: A PEP was a British savings scheme (Personal Equity Plan).
explanation.definitionFit: A pep talk is a short speech meant to encourage and motivate.

clue.text: Attic I converted

parts.note: Attic is the Greek of Athens, so the letter I turned into the Greek alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, the counterpart of I; also a tiny amount.

clue.text: What produced hang-ups, bitterness and cries of pain?

parts.note: gall is bitterness, rancour
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: What caused someone's neuroses: resentment and yelps of hurt?
explanation.walkthrough: 'hang-ups' suggests psychological problems; read literally, it is people being hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbet is where executions by hanging were carried out.

clue.text: Scarcely able to make a difficult shot

definitions.meaning: in difficulty, struggling to do something
a tough throw in the shot-put

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means struggling to manage, and read literally it is a strenuous throw of the shot.

clue.text: Final part of a disco dance

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The last section of a nightclub routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music, its finale.

clue.text: Joy has kinsman decapitated

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: a kinsman is a relation

explanation.surface: Happiness at a relative's beheading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' removes the first letter R from RELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness or exhilaration.

clue.text: Personally act to get a non-guilty verdict

definitions.meaning: to conduct yourself, perform in a certain way
to clear yourself in court, literally

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to behave or perform, and read literally it is to be cleared of a charge.

clue.text: Looking young, you and I shall get waited on in advance

parts.note: we'll is short for we shall, you and I shall
pre- is a prefix meaning before, in advance
served means waited on, as at table

explanation.surface: Two people expect to be served early to stay youthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you and I shall' contracts to WE'LL; the apostrophe is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-preserved describes someone who looks younger than their age.

clue.text: Funds to establish a mine in California

indicators.note: in places the phrase a mine within the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Money is needed to start up a mining operation in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A PIT inside CAL, the abbreviation for California.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is money available for investment, a stock of funds.

clue.text: Embarrassed by record of bureaucratic constraint

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: Someone blushes at a document detailing official obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is the idiom for excessive official rules and paperwork.

clue.text: Raised a small tree

parts.note: something raised is up
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone lifted a little sapling.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a poisonous tropical Asian tree of the fig family.

clue.text: Manage to garage fashionable car

indicators.note: to garage something is to house it, so one word is stored inside another

parts.note: to manage is to cope
U means upper-class, socially acceptable, hence fashionable

explanation.surface: A driver contrives to park a stylish motor in the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to garage' puts U, the old 'upper-class' tag, inside COPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupé is a two-door car with a fixed roof.

clue.text: Plant makes a large number sick

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A factory makes many people ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill is a factory or industrial plant.

clue.text: Some admit King George was mad

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word takes another inside it

parts.note: any means some
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A few concede that King George was insane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' tempts as the historical King George's madness, but it means cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in the American sense of cross or furious.

clue.text: Painter leaves mobile home in Ireland

indicators.note: leaves means the painter goes away from the vehicle

parts.note: a caravan is a mobile home
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist moves out of a trailer in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: RA (Royal Academician) is the stock crossword painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavan is a county and town in the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Money in the till thanks to Cambridge college

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
King's is a college of Cambridge University

explanation.surface: Cash in the register comes courtesy of a university college.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you; KING'S College is in Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the receipts of a shop or business.

clue.text: Tutor acquires suite with hesitation

indicators.note: acquires says the first word takes on the next piece at its end

parts.note: a suite is a retinue of attendants, a train
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A teacher gets a set of rooms but dithers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suite' here is a retinue of followers, not rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a coach or instructor.

clue.text: Remedy a lack of rhythm

parts.note: no expresses absence, a lack of
a strum is a rhythmic strumming of strings

explanation.surface: A cure for someone with no sense of rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine or pet cure.

clue.text: Stool is adjusted when he gives a piano recital

indicators.note: adjusted means the letters are rearranged, like a piano seat set to height

explanation.surface: A pianist adjusts his stool before performing.
explanation.definitionFit: A soloist is a performer playing alone, as in a solo recital.

clue.text: Mother takes in head-dress from eastern sage

indicators.note: takes in means one word contains the other

parts.note: mama is mother
a hat is a head-dress

explanation.surface: A mother accepts a turban from an oriental wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an Indian title for a revered holy man, as with Gandhi.

clue.text: About to take young ladies out of lectures

parts.note: C stands for circa, about
lasses are girls, young ladies

explanation.surface: Girls are taken out of lectures for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Classes are teaching sessions, like lectures.

clue.text: Winning journalist ate like a horse

parts.note: champ, short for champion, the winner
ED is the abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A victorious reporter ate greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ate like a horse' suggests greed, but champing is a horse's noisy chewing.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to chew noisily, as a horse at its bit.

clue.text: A fair number always accommodated by Sarah

indicators.note: accommodated by means held inside the next word

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah
ever means always

explanation.surface: Many people have always stayed with Sarah.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means more than two but not many, a moderate number.

clue.text: Only it is trodden underfoot

definitions.meaning: the underside of the foot or shoe

explanation.definitionFit: One word means only and also the bottom of the foot, which treads the ground.

clue.text: Talk about English fraud

indicators.note: about places the talk around the letter for English

parts.note: to talk is to chat

explanation.surface: Gossip about an English swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat is a swindler or a dishonest trick.

clue.text: Insist that small road goes to the right

indicators.note: goes to the means one piece is followed by the next

parts.note: AVE is the abbreviation for avenue, a road

explanation.surface: Someone maintains that the lane bends rightwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly, to assert.

clue.text: Give orders to S African security men

definitions.meaning: to order people about, to dominate
the old Bureau of State Security in South Africa

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to order about, and also names South Africa's apartheid-era secret police.

clue.text: Some divorced couples do

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a portion and a verb for separating, as divorcing couples do.

clue.text: Arranged for hooligan to get help in

indicators.note: get help in says the support goes inside the yob

parts.note: a lout is a hooligan
aid means help

explanation.surface: A thug is organised to get assistance brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid out means set out or arranged, as a display.

clue.text: The couple lied. That is plain

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair, a couple
a lied is a German art song, an air
ie stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Two people told untruths, and that's the plain fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' is not a fib but the German word for a song, an AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a vast grassy plain of North America.

clue.text: Not moving away from a market stall

definitions.text: Not moving away from a market stall

parts.words: Not moving away from a market stall
parts.note: a trader staying put by a stand at market; read as a phrase it describes total lack of motion

explanation.surface: A shopper lingers by a market booth.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AT A STAND STILL, it pictures someone motionless at a stall.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for completely stopped or stalled.
